classification.difficultyReason: Convert square metres to square centimetres, model outer frame dimensions, use a general quadratic-solving method and select and round the positive width.

content.prompt:
Nick and Chloe want to surround their 60 by 80 cm wedding photo with a frame of equal width. The resulting photo and frame is to be covered by a $1\text{ m}^2$ sheet of glass.

Find the width of the frame, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.short: $-35+5\sqrt{101}\text{ cm}\approx15.25\text{ cm}$. Use $(80+2x)(60+2x)=10000$, where $x$ is the frame width in centimetres.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the frame width in centimetres. The outer dimensions are $(80+2x)$ cm and $(60+2x)$ cm, and $1\text{ m}^2=10000\text{ cm}^2$.

$$\begin{align*}(80+2x)(60+2x)&=10000\\4x^2+280x+4800&=10000\\4x^2+280x-5200&=0\\x^2+70x-1300&=0\\x&=\frac{-70\pm\sqrt{70^2-4(1)(-1300)}}{2}\\x&=\frac{-70\pm\sqrt{10100}}{2}\\x&=-35\pm5\sqrt{101}.\end{align*}$$

The negative root is unsuitable because the frame width must be positive. Hence the width is $-35+5\sqrt{101}\text{ cm}\approx15.25\text{ cm}$, correct to 2 decimal places.
